transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-20
Start: 15:00 PDT
Duration: 58 minutes
Attendees: Ava (Redwood AE), Marcus (Redwood SE), Dana (Redwood CSM), Liam (Pegasus CISO), Priya (Sec Eng), Ethan (IT Ops), Sofia (Compliance)

Auto-generated summary (may be rough): review of controls and trust center access requested. Discussed KMS flow and evidence ingestion API, asked about log retention and SIEM.

--- Transcript body ---
[00:00] Ava: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call, then we'll jump into the controls inventory sync.
[00:12] Liam: Hey, Liam here. Good morning.
[00:15] Priya: Priya on my side.
[00:18] Ethan: Ethan here.
[00:20] Sofia: Sofia, compliance.
[00:22] Ava: Great. Marcus, do you want to frame the artifacts we'll share?
[00:28] Marcus: Yeah, sure. So, uh, we have our SOC 2 Type II report, ISO gap summary, and the Trust Center portal. I'll send the read-only link after the call. There's also a short controls mapping spreadsheet that maps our controls to common SOC 2 criteria, um, and ISO clauses.
[00:45] Priya: When you say "Trust Center portal" is that the same as the one in the docs link we saw? I saw a drive link in the invite but wanted to confirm.
[00:52] Ava: Yes, that's the same. Link will be, uh, redwood.ai/trustcenter/pegasus, we'll add you as a read-only viewer. Some artifacts are downloadable, some are view-only because of sensitivity.
[01:05] Liam: One of our big asks — and this is the main reason for the call — is clarity on encryption at rest and key custody. We need to understand KMS flows, whether we can bring our keys, and HSM options.
[01:18] Marcus: Totally. So high level, hosted API uses Redwood-managed keys by default. For Dedicated or Private we support customer-managed keys: Cloud KMS integrations (GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault) and for on-prem we can integrate HSMs via KMIP or, um, through a vault proxy. There is also an option for a bring-your-own-key pattern where the root keys stay in your KMS and Redwood holds only ephemeral wrappers.
[01:44] Priya: That's helpful. Two follow-ups: 1) does Redwood support envelope encryption with customer KMS? 2) can you share the Terraform snippets or example config?
[01:52] Marcus: Yes to envelope encryption. We have example Terraform and deployment snippets. I'll put the snippets in the shared folder and attach a short diagram showing the flow: client -> Redwood control plane (no key material) -> KMS sign/unwrap -> runtime. The exact flow varies slightly between our hosted tier and dedicated/private because of network topology.
[02:14] Ethan: On the logs side: we need to forward audit logs to our SIEM, and retention is negotiable but we need at least 2 years for some artifacts. How do you support streaming audit logs or batch export?
[02:24] Marcus: We support several patterns: real-time forwarding via syslog/Logstash endpoint, S3 export for bulk retention, and an audit API for pull-based retrieval. There are also webhook options. Note that streaming has a small ingestion latency and we can provide signatures for log integrity.
[02:40] Sofia: Does Redwood preserve user-level audit trails for admin actions? For SOC 2 evidence we need detailed change history.
[02:47] Marcus: Yes, we log admin actions, model deployments, config changes, and access events. The audit logs contain actor, timestamp, resource and action. Small caveat: some low-level infra noise is aggregated; we can provide raw logs on request for audits.
[03:05] Priya: About RBAC and SSO — we use Okta and SCIM provisioning. How mature is the SCIM sync and role mapping?
[03:13] Dana: Our SCIM implementation supports groups and attribute mapping; roles can be synced and we support role-based policies in the console. There's also SAML for SSO and we can enable MFA via your IdP. For finer-grain access we support API keys per service and token scoping.
[03:32] Liam: If we need separation by business unit, can we enforce strict tenant-level RBAC and prevent cross-tenant metadata leakage?
[03:39] Marcus: Yes, isolation is enforced at the namespace level for Dedicated and Private. For hosted, we offer logical tenancy and strict RBAC but for the highest assurance you'll likely want Dedicated or Private with network isolation.
[03:54] Priya: We have a question on data residency. Our EU customers' PII must remain in eu-west-1. Can you guarantee region pinning?
[04:02] Marcus: We support region pinning in Dedicated and Private. For hosted API we can route to region-specific endpoints but there are edge cases for backups and DR which we should clarify — backups for hosted may exist in another region unless you contract for dedicated residency. We'll capture that as a requirement.
[04:20] Liam: Ok, so likely we'll need Dedicated. We're also evaluating cost tradeoffs.
[04:26] Ava: Totally expected. We'll provide a cost delta and the performance/latency SLOs per option.
[04:33] Priya: Back to logs — you mentioned signatures for log integrity. Is that an HMAC or an external signing?
[04:40] Marcus: Currently HMAC signatures with key rotation; for higher assurance we can support an append-only ledger with an external signing HSM, that's part of our advanced compliance package.
[04:50] Ethan: Great, would be good to see a POC of log streaming to our Splunk instance. We can open a dev index for this.
[04:58] Ava: We'll set that up. Marcus, follow-up?
[05:02] Marcus: I'll propose a lightweight POC: enable log forwarding to a dev Splunk endpoint, demonstrate audit event fidelity for a week, then push/export S3 snapshots.
[05:12] Sophia: small note — sometimes the transcription mangles our product names like, uh, "KV cache" becomes "K V cash" in the doc. 
[05:18] Marcus: Ha, yeah Fireflies does that, sorry.
[05:22] Liam: Quick tangent: for control mapping we want to map your controls to our internal control IDs. Do you have a machine readable mapping?
[05:30] Marcus: We have a CSV mapping control id -> control name -> SOC 2 criteria -> ISO clause. We can also export as a spreadsheet. We'll annotate which controls are implemented at the platform level versus customer responsibility (shared responsibility).
[05:44] Priya: Will you mark the evidence artifacts for each control? E.g., for access reviews, where is the proof?
[05:50] Marcus: Yes, the spreadsheet includes links to artifacts in the Trust Center — e.g., access review reports, penetration test summary, encryption architecture, vulnerability management pipeline evidence.
[06:02] Ava: Let's walk through a short sample control: Access provisioning and deprovisioning. Marcus?
[06:10] Marcus: Sure. Provisioning follows SCIM from your IdP to Redwood; deprovisioning is immediate for SAML/SCIM events. We also retain a provisioning log entry and snapshot user states daily for replay. The control evidence is the provisioning logs plus the SCIM change events and the audit export.
[06:32] Sofia: For SOC 2 auditors we need a historical sample for the last 12 months. Can you produce that?
[06:40] Marcus: Yes, we can produce historical logs for a rolling 12 months depending on retention policy — if you need more we'll export to S3 for long term retention. There may be cost for extended retention.
[06:52] Priya: Anything about endpoint security? We run host-based detection and want to ensure no lateral access from Redwood-managed infra.
[06:59] Marcus: We operate strict network segmentation. For dedicated/private the runtime sits in your VPC or on-prem and network controls are enforced by you. For hosted we use isolated runtime sandboxes, process-level isolation, and continuous scanning. We'll share our infra hardening doc.
[07:18] Ethan: Are there any known gaps in scope for ISO 27001 alignment? We have internal checklist items that need a bridge.
[07:26] Marcus: Our ISO alignment note shows a few gaps that are typically customer-owned — things like physical security of customer on-prem systems or corporate HR policies. We'll mark each gap and propose mitigations if needed.
[07:39] Priya: One subtle point — for log integrity we need non-repudiation of admin changes. How do you handle log tamper-proofing?
[07:47] Marcus: We use append-only storage with tamper detect checksums. For audit-grade we can push signed digests to a third-party witness or to your internal ledger. That's optional and has an operational cost.
[08:02] Liam: Ok, good. Let's talk timeline. We're aiming for a SOC 2 readiness review by Q3 and a potential procurement decision by end of Q3. That means we want a POC and Trust Center access within two weeks.
[08:15] Ava: We can meet that. We'll share trust center access today or tomorrow and Marcus will deliver the KMS diagram and the log-forwarding POC plan.
[08:25] Priya: For the KMS diagram, can you also show the fallback behavior if KMS is unavailable? e.g., request retries, circuit breakers, and how cached KV is handled?
[08:34] Marcus: Yes, we'll document failure modes: request retries, exponential backoff, and a conservative cached ephemeral key approach for short tails. We'll also show how we revoke caches in case of compromise.
[08:47] Ethan: We'll need support for Splunk HEC and a syslog sink — can you confirm HEC token rotation?
[08:55] Marcus: HEC tokens can be rotated and we support token scoping per index. For syslog we support TLS and mutual TLS if required.
[09:06] Sofia: Any questions from Redwood?
[09:09] Ava: No, just to confirm next steps and owners. We'll also attach the controls mapping CSV.
[09:16] Liam: Sounds good.
[09:18] Priya: One last note: our legal team will want an updated DPA with data residency terms. Who handles that?
[09:24] Ava: Our legal team handles DPA; I'll introduce you to our contract lead and share the standard DPA. We can add residency clauses as appendices.
[09:33] Liam: Ok thanks.
[09:35] Ava: Recap: Trust Center access, KMS/HSM diagram and TF snippet, SIEM POC scheduled, controls mapping CSV sent. We'll follow up with calendar invites for the POC kickoff.
[09:46] Marcus: I'll assign the technical tasks and share the repository link.
[09:50] Ethan: Thanks everyone.
[09:52] Meeting end notes: Attendees agreed to the POC. Expect artifacts in 48 hours (Trust Center + diagrams) and POC kickoff next week.
[09:58] End of transcript.
